_note: Machine-checkable form of the Deliverable Quality Bar. Left unchecked: (1) live-interview mode ('in live mode, correctly identifies value-laden language and generates targeted probes'), (2) post-interview mode ('clearly distinguishes descriptive from normative findings') and (3) the values portrait bar. All three need a participant quote or transcript as input, and none of the three eval prompts supplies one: they all ask for a Protocol Design run. A check on them would pass vacuously. (4) 'Domain-Specific Questions when domain is specified' has no structural presence check because no eval prompt names one of the five Investigation domains, so a section_present would either always pass (conditional never triggered) or demand a section the brief did not ask for; the named-technical-questions bar is checked semantically on whatever domain section the output chooses to write. (5) Counts use the skill's own wording: at least 8 follow-ups, at least 2 construct-building probes, 4-6 covert categories. Outputs differ in layout (one protocol, or one per stakeholder group), so counts read the first matching section, which is enough to meet 'at least N' for one protocol; the per-stakeholder repeats are not required.

semantic.bar: contains at least 2 construct-building probes with explicit instructions about which value words to watch for
semantic.instructions: Does `items[{i}]` tell the interviewer which value-laden words to watch for and how to probe them?

criteria.true: Names example value words (such as 'unfair', 'wrong', 'manipulative', 'surveillance', 'trust') and tells the interviewer to mirror the participant's exact word and ask what they mean by it.
criteria.false: A generic instruction to 'probe deeper' or 'ask why' with no value words named, or it paraphrases the participant's word instead of mirroring it.

semantic.bar: lists 4–6 covert categories phrased as research intentions, not direct questions
semantic.instructions: Is the covert category in `items[{i}]` a research intention rather than a question to put to the participant?

criteria.true: States what the researcher wants to understand (often 'I want to understand X without asking Y'), as an aim of the research.
criteria.false: Is itself a question addressed to the participant, or a gotcha about what the participant is hiding.

semantic.bar: identifying proxy-variable harms, discoverability risk, aggregation harms, and retaliation risk for the populations being researched
semantic.instructions: Does the row in `items[{i}]` name a specific population and a harm particular to it, with the protocol question that surfaces or blocks it?

criteria.true: Names a specific group (for example 'applicants from low-income zip codes' or 'junior editors who report to the CTO') and a concrete non-obvious harm for that group, and links it to protocol questions.
criteria.false: Names only 'users' or 'everyone', or gives a generic harm such as 'privacy risk' with no link to the protocol.

semantic.bar: halt protocol — all named, not implied
semantic.instructions: Are the guardrails in `items[{i}]` stated as specific decisions for this research rather than as good intentions?

criteria.true: Each guardrail commits to a particular choice: who interviews whom and the power gap it creates, where recordings are kept and who can see them, how long they are kept and how a participant can redact, what consent covers, named steps for trauma-aware framing, and named conditions that stop the interview.
criteria.false: Guardrails are generic reassurances such as 'we will protect confidentiality' or 'we will be sensitive', or some of the five are missing or only implied.

semantic.bar: when a domain is specified, includes named technical questions specific to that domain (proxy variables, named fairness metrics, appeal mechanisms, etc.)
semantic.instructions: Are the domain-specific questions in `items[{i}]` technical and specific to the domain, beyond what a general values interview would ask?

criteria.true: Asks about named technical specifics for the domain, for example proxy variables used as inputs, training data provenance, named fairness metrics, monitoring cadence, who can challenge a decision, appeal mechanisms, rollback criteria or veto power.
criteria.false: Repeats general values or experience questions with no technical or domain-specific content.

semantic.bar: provides interview sequencing rationale with dependency tree
semantic.instructions: Does `items[{i}]` give an order for interviewing the groups in this research and say why the order matters for what each later interview can ask?

criteria.true: Names the specific participant groups in this research, puts them in an order, and explains what each earlier interview gives the later ones (a dependency), for example hearing impacted users before the people who built the system.
criteria.false: Lists the groups with no reason for the order, or gives only generic advice that does not use this research's participants.

semantic.bar: opens with a direct answer to the decision or question the user asked, which the rest of the output supports
semantic.instructions: Does `items[{i}]` answer the question the user asked, with its main reason?

criteria.true: Two to four sentences that give a recommendation or verdict about how to run these interviews and the main reason for it.
criteria.false: Restates the task, announces what follows, or gives no recommendation or reason.

semantic.bar: lists the figures and facts about the user's situation it relies on in an Evidence Ledger, typed user-supplied / sourced / assumption / unknown, and invents none
semantic.instructions: Does the Basis column of `items[{i}]` avoid citing a skill, its rules or its box?

criteria.true: Every Basis names the brief, a paper, a URL or model knowledge, and invents no figure about the user's situation.
criteria.false: Some Basis cites a skill, its workflow or its rules (for example 'the skill workflow section G'), or a row states an invented figure as fact.
